text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: ap-northeast-1 GPU pool experiencing sustained kernel preemption -> p50 token latency +180ms over baseline, error rate up 3x. Autoscaler reports 68% available capacity but pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Investigating.
alex: seeing the same in dashboards. KV-cache miss rate spiked too. RTT from edge -> model nodes jumped.
maya: any recent infra deploys in ap-northeast? I don't see any matching job in deploy history.
jordan: none from infra. ML did a model rollout two hours ago but it was a non-quantized variant; shouldn't cause kernel preemptions. tagging @ml-team for visibility.
alex: priority is to reduce customer-facing latency. Suggest manual weight shift away from ap-northeast to na-east-1 and eu-west-1, keep a small residual weight for warm cache (10%).
sam: agree. We should avoid a hard drain to prevent thundering cache misses. Proposed weights: ap-northeast=0.10, na-east=0.60, eu-west=0.30. Worst-case egress cost delta ~+$2.8k/day, acceptable for incident window.
oncall-ryan: I'm on it, holding a manual override. Executing route change now.
oncall-ryan: running command:
```
# gslbctl v2
gslbctl set-weights --policy live-routing --region ap-northeast-1=0.10 --region na-east-1=0.60 --region eu-west-1=0.30 --reason "ap-northeast kernel preemptions"
```
oncall-ryan: API returned 202, propagation started. TTLs are 30s so changes should be visible within ~60s.
maya: watching metrics. p50 dropping already from +180ms -> +90ms in 45s. error rate trending down.
alex: good. Can we also temporarily increase ap-northeast GPU node reboot grace and disable auto-evict to stabilize pods? Might prevent repeated restarts.
jordan: making kube-sched tweak: patching cluster-config, set `max-surge` to 0 and `gracePeriodSeconds` to 120 for model pods in ap-northeast. Applying now.
ops-bot: SYSTEM: Route change propagated to 72% of edges. Health checks for ap-northeast still flapping but request volume is reduced.
sam: cost/latency note: if this holds, we should run a prioritized backlog for kernel-preemption fix with infra/driver team tomorrow. Also consider warming a smaller quantized variant in-region to absorb traffic without driver churn.
alex: agreed. For now, keep the soft weights for 30 minutes, then reassess. If ap-northeast stabilizes, we will ramp back gradually (10% increments every 5m).
oncall-ryan: ack. I'll update the incident doc and ping customers with SLO-sensitive traffic routes if this impacts them.
maya: p50 back within +30ms of baseline. leaving 10% to warm cache as planned. nice work everyone :thumbsup:
ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: manual routing override active by user oncall-ryan; incident ticket #INC-2026-412 created and linked."
